# Vendored crates

`ps5upload-fpkg` (FPKG builder and readers) and `ps5upload-pkg` (UFS2 reader, package
inspection), taken from ps5upload with a small local patch series on top.

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload |
| Tag / commit | `v12.6.30` / `4174eee` ("12.6.30: phone Files, Play Together on a TV, unpacked packages, PS4 update version, audit fixes (#938)") |
| Path upstream | `engine/crates/ps5upload-fpkg`, `engine/crates/ps5upload-pkg` |
| License | GPL-3.0-or-later (see `LICENSE-ps5upload`, and the note below) |
| Edition | 2021, as upstream, on purpose: it keeps the diff to upstream small |

The trees here are upstream plus every patch in `patches/` except 0021 (lzma-rust2, below), in order. Nothing else differs.

`LICENSE-UnRAR.txt` and `LICENSE-UnRAR-exception.md` are not vendored code: UnRAR's license and the
GPLv3 §7 permission for the UnRAR source that `unrar_sys` (crates.io) builds into every target. The
release scripts copy both into each package.

## Patches

Paths in each patch are relative to this folder (`a/ps5upload-fpkg/...`). Each patch carries its
own tests. Upstream took eleven earlier patches by v7.0.22 (reader empty dirs, reader bounds, Kraken
descriptor bounds, `SourceTree: Send`, `.Trashes`, strict names, no silent UFS2 drops, header bounds,
`fakelib2`, exFAT cluster runs, public `imports_ampr`), and by v12.6.30 these of the v7.0.22 series
(numbers as they were then): 0012 (sampled self-check: upstream's `BuildControl::sample`, which
samples the data blocks and the `playgo-chunk.crc` table and always sweeps the format's own
blocks), 0014 (CRC-32C slicing by 8), 0016 and 0030 (a packed source's own `ampr_emu.index` kept:
upstream's `source::packed_kind`, LZ4 or zstd, any letter case of the index name), 0027, 0028 and
0029 (patch and PSVIETHOA descriptor walks, the shuffle table, 128/136 KiB blocks, PFSv3
shuffles; upstream carries the same tests), 0031 (`is_safe_child_name` as an expression; its test
covered the UFS2 extractor, which Forge doesn't use). Those were dropped, not rebased; 0024
(a test comment) is folded into 0007. Upstream also took parts of 0005 and 0008 and the
"Sony's no-data stretches" half of 0007; those patches keep only the rest (rows below).

| Patch | What it does |
|---|---|
| `0001-cargo-pins.patch` | Pins `edition`, `license` and `version` in both `Cargo.toml`s instead of inheriting them from upstream's workspace. Leaves off flate2's `zlib-rs` feature, which upstream turns on for its own `.ffpfsc` writer (Forge doesn't use it): features unify, so it would also move Forge's own `.ffpfsc` writer off miniz_oxide. Drops the `libdeflater` dependency (libdeflate's C, upstream's `.ffpfsc` block encoder): it doesn't build for the PS5 payload, whose SDK clang lacks the AVX-VNNI and VPCLMULQDQ intrinsics libdeflate's x86 code calls; `ffpfsc_block`'s two encoders become flate2 ones (levels above 9 taken as 9), code Forge doesn't call. Removes `examples/exfat_read_bench.rs`, which needs blake3's `rayon` feature (upstream's workspace has it, Forge's doesn't). |
| `0002-build-from-source-tree.patch` | Splits the build into `build::prepare(tree, request, control) -> Prepared` and `build::write_package(prepared, tree, out_file, out_path, progress, control)`, which writes into a caller-owned file (no `.partial`, no rename) and verifies it. `Prepared` exposes the effective manifest (`ManifestEntry { path, size, origin: Origin }`), the container-only artwork, empty dirs, content id, warnings, estimated size (now covering the container's payloads, per-block tables, per-file/per-directory records and the `param.json` fields `pfsimage.xml` repeats), `generated_bytes` and `read_range` (the packaged bytes of any manifest file). Files read whole (`param.json`, container payloads) are bounded to 256 MiB together, by declared size, before any is read, on top of upstream's per-file `source::read_small` caps; upstream's cap for an asset index read whole (`source::MAX_INDEX_BYTES`, also what readiness reads a game's `ampr_emu.index` within) is 256 MiB here, not 512, as the old 0016 bounded it: a job stays within 512 MiB. `prepare` reads the tree it is given: upstream's `BuildRequest::reader` and its fake-signing of plain ELF executables (`fself::wrap`) need the tree by value and run in `build` only (Forge unpacks and signs before). `build`, `build_controlled` and `build_in_memory` run on the two, with upstream's `finish::rename`. |
| `0003-production-request.patch` | `BuildRequest::production(source, output_dir)`: PlaintextNoAuth, Kraken, Balanced, Stored metadata, default chunks, and `env_overrides: false`, so no `PS5UPLOAD_FPKG_*` variable is read, neither in the constructor nor during the build (`PARAM_FILE`, `SPOOL_DIR`, `DRM_TYPE`, `KRAKEN_STORE`). Upstream's `kraken::Level::Stored` (every block raw, the fallback for consoles that refuse a compressed package) is the one route to a stored image: `KRAKEN_STORE=1` maps to it only with `env_overrides`. `BuildRequest::new` is unchanged, except that a `PARAM_FILE` replacement is held to the same 256 MiB bound. |
| `0004-compression-thread-cap.patch` | `BuildRequest::threads: Option<usize>` (`None`/`Some(0)` = all the pool may have, larger caps clamp to it) sizes the Kraken compression pool, within upstream's `workshop::workshop_threads()` (every core unless its process-wide gentle mode or thread cap says fewer; Forge sets neither). The output is the same for every cap. |
| `0005-cancellation.patch` | Upstream checks the cancel flag in the compressor, the stream writer and the verifier (every 256 blocks), but answers a `Format` error there ("cancelled", "the build was cancelled"). Here every stop is `Error::Cancelled`; `verify::verify_file_controlled(PkgFile, passcode, seed, cancel, progress)` verifies an open package (upstream's `verify_streaming_controlled` opens a path, and now goes through it), so `write_package` verifies through the caller's handle; the flag is checked on every block of the sweep and of the `playgo-chunk.crc` table (`si::chunk_crc_table_controlled`); `write_package` and `build` check it again once a verification passes, so a stop asked for during its last read is never published. `prepare` checks it after each stage callback, per file and between container payload reads; the streaming writer per data and metadata block, between sections and before the final sync. Every check goes through upstream's `workshop::checkpoint` (a paused job waits there). Not covered: `source::readiness`'s bounded AMPR scan (at most ~80 MiB read). |
| `0006-ufs2-range-reads.patch` | UFS2 `read_range` reads blocks that lie back to back on disk as one run (one seek and one read, bounded by the requested length; a hole, a jump or a bad pointer ends the run and is met next, as before), and `block_ptr` reads a whole pointer block once and keeps the last one per indirection depth, keyed by fragment, instead of a seek and an 8-byte read per level per block. Found on hardware: a `.ffpkg` → `.exfat` conversion of an 87 GB image ran at ~105 MB/s on a PS5, ~6 syscalls per 64 KiB block. An 8 MiB read of a contiguous file is now 2 reads at 64 KiB blocks (single indirect; was 256) and 3 at 16 KiB blocks in the double-indirect range (was 1536). Bytes and errors match a block at a time, except that a pointer block cut short by a truncated image now fails even when the entries a range needs are present (`read_file` already did). Every byte offset `read_range` and `block_ptr` compute from a pointer is checked (fragment × size, + offset, + length) and must end inside the declared image size, else `BlockOutOfRange`: with a forged `fs_size`, a huge pointer's saturated offset wrapped to byte 0 in release builds (and panicked with overflow checks on). |
| `0007-kraken-sparse-extents.patch` | Upstream's `kraken_image::describe` steps over a `fidx` entry of type 0x40 before the mount's end (a stretch with no stored data, Sony's Astro Bot has 1,988) and returns no block for it; Forge's reader needs blocks that tile the mount, so here such a sparse extent comes back as zero blocks of at most 256 KiB, none crossing a boundary (`stored_len` 0, `DescribedBlock::is_sparse`), which `decode_described` decodes to zeros, and `layout`'s read-back check leaves them out. Upstream's rules stay: an ordinary entry at the same offset wins, and a block before a sparse stretch is cut short only by a record that doesn't start where it leaves off (gaps stepped over; this removed Forge's old ponytail). Added: a boundary table whose mount end disagrees with the ublock count (ceil(mount / 256 KiB)) is refused, so a tiny descriptor cannot ask for millions of zero blocks; a real record whose stored span is empty, and a block stored in no bytes without the whole sparse sentinel, are refused; the next boundary and the sparse extents are looked up by binary search, so the walk is O(n log n) (upstream scans the boundaries for every record; 100,000 boundaries took 3.9 s that way, a forged descriptor of ~5.6 M about 1.5 h; 4 M now take 0.24 s). Found in a third-party package: a 256 KiB hole between two files, which shifted every later block. Upstream's gap tests now expect the zero blocks. |
| `0008-kraken-entropy-halves.patch` | Upstream decodes a non-LZ half stored shorter than its logical size as one bare entropy array (`Half::Entropy`, its #493). Kept from the old patch: `decode_half` requires the excess streams to meet, a single-symbol Huffman table must fill its body exactly, and a block of at most 128 KiB with bytes past its even half is refused; the mode bits' documentation; tests that the literal-mode bits don't apply to a non-LZ half and that a third-party package's block (an LZ even half, a bare zero odd half) decodes. |
| `0009-pic-png-entries.patch` | `pic1.png` (0x1006) and `pic2.png` (0x2040) join `PRESENTATION`, `CONTAINER_ONLY` and the system general digest (`ids::SYSTEM_DIGEST_IDS`, id order): a folder that has them builds a package that carries them as container entries, like `pic0.png`, and a reader that merges the container gets them back under `sce_sys/`. A third-party package carries both, outside its image, and its system digest matches only with both in it (before, our verifier reported that digest as wrong). Ids and names from that package's name table. |
| `0010-kraken-decode-speed.patch` | Decoder speed, same bytes: a match copies eight bytes at a time and delta literals add eight at a time (every distance is at least 8, so a word never reads a byte not yet written); the Huffman reader refills a whole word while eight bytes of its stream are left (byte by byte at the end, as before) and fills its output by stream rotation instead of `i % 3`; `decode_described` decodes from borrowed halves (`kraken::decode_parts` over `kraken::Part`, a borrowed `Half`, entropy halves included) instead of copying each into a `Half`. With the reader's parallel decode this took a 188 GB third-party package from 403 to 1,440 MB/s (4 MiB reads, 14 cores); every one of its 521 files hashes as before. |
| `0011-parallel-write-and-sweep.patch` | The write stage of a compressed build reads its spooled image back 8 MiB at a time and digests (and, for a native image, encrypts) the blocks on every core (`stream::digest_blocks`), each block's SHA3 taken once for both `imagedigs` and the block list (it was taken twice, one block at a time). The verifier's outer-block sweep (`verify::failing_blocks`, over upstream's sampled runs when a seed is given) and its `playgo-chunk.crc` recomputation (`si::chunk_crc_table_controlled`) read 8 MiB at a time and work on every core. Same bytes, digests and verdicts. Found on an 89 GB build: after a ~4 min compress, the write and verify stages ran on one core. |
| `0012-kraken-skip-hopeless-search.patch` | The Kraken encoder skips its match search for a half it could not keep compressed (it keeps one only when it saves 2%), storing it raw at once: the half's byte entropy and that of its delta literals (each byte less the one 8 back, the distance literal mode 0 starts with) are both over 7.9 bits, and an estimate of what it could save (order-0 coding plus the matches a one-probe hash scan finds, priced by the encoder's own `gain`) is under 1%. A heuristic, not a proof: it can store raw a half the search would have kept (one whose savings come from deltas at a distance only a match sets, or from matches the probe misses); such a half is valid, only larger. Every level; the format is unchanged (raw halves are what the encoder already wrote for incompressible data). A test keeps a delta-coded half (≈8-bit bytes, no repeats, half its size as delta literals) searched and compressed at every level. Found on a 9.2 GB game with large compressed audio: 47% of the fast level's CPU went to the 34,071 of 74,725 halves that end up raw; the scan skipped 31,188 of them, the compress stage went from 33 to 24 s (14 cores) and 4 halves the search kept (each saving 2.0–2.6%) are now raw, +12 KB; at the balanced level 1 of a sampled 9,339 halves changed, +2.8 KB. |
| `0013-kraken-file-sha3-thread.patch` | `kraken_image::compress` takes each file's SHA3 on a thread of its own (`hash_files`), fed the blocks in file order through a bounded channel (32 blocks, at most 8 MiB; the block buffers move, nothing is copied), instead of on the thread that reads the source, keeps the compression pool fed and lays out the blocks, where it took ~40% of that thread's time. Same digests, in the same order (a test compares them with each file's SHA3); an error or a panic in the pipeline closes the channel, which ends the hasher. On a 9.2 GB game converted from its `.pkg` (14 cores, fast level, Forge's 4 MiB read-ahead): compress 28.2 to 26.2 s. |
| `0014-packed-source-index-tests.patch` | Tests only (upstream has the behaviour, see above), through `prepare`, the path Forge builds by: an LZ4-packed and a zstd-packed source keep their own `ampr_emu.index` byte for byte (`Origin::Source`, nothing generated); without the pack magic the index is generated anew; a packed source whose index is missing or unreadable is refused; a listed manifest whose first bytes can't be read fails with that read's error, never "not packed". |
| `0015-ampr-scan-once.patch` | A `.pkg` build scanned `eboot.bin` for `libSceAmpr` (`source::imports_ampr`: up to 16 MiB of the module, its headers and the load segment holding its dynamic section, up to ~80 MiB in all) three times: in the caller's `readiness`, in `prepare`'s own `readiness`, and again where `prepare` decides on `ampr_emu.index`. From a folder that is cached reads; from an archive source (measured on a 7,169-file `.rar`) each scan re-reads the module through the decoder. `Readiness` now carries the answer (`imports_ampr: bool`), `source::readiness_with(tree, Some(answer))` skips the scan, and `BuildRequest::imports_ampr: Option<bool>` hands a caller's answer to `prepare` (`None`, set by every constructor, scans once); `prepare` takes its index decision from its own `readiness`. Upstream's readiness checks a packed game's index whatever its eboot imports. One test: told `Some(false)`, an AMPR module gets no generated index. |
| `0016-prepare-progress.patch` | `BuildControl::files: Option<&mut dyn FnMut(Stage, u64, u64)>` counts `prepare`'s two per-file passes as `(stage, done, total)`, in files visited: the SELF header read of every file in `Stage::Check` and the 4-byte module mark of every planned file in `Stage::Plan`, the files a pass skips without a read included (`fakelib/` and under 32 bytes in check; generated and under 4 bytes in plan, now one loop over the plan with `PlannedFile::may_be_module`, which `Plan::mark_modules` shares), so `done` ends at `total`. Called at a pass's first file, every 256 files and at its last (`done == total`), so a quarter of a million files make about a thousand calls; the last only when not stopped (the flag is checked first). Check reads the headers through upstream's `SourceTree::read_heads` (a folder opens several at once), 256 files a call; upstream's walked-bytes reports of that pass through `bytes` are sent only when `files` is `None`. Found on a 7,169-file `.rar` source: the two passes took ~33 s and a caller had nothing to show but the stage. One test: 600 extra files, all too short for check's read and half for plan's, both passes counted 0, 256, 512, ... and their total, and a stop during plan ends its count without the total. |
| `0017-hold-metadata-region-once.patch` | A streaming build held the inner image's metadata region (64 KiB per directory, plus one per ~390 files) four times through the compress stage: `Metadata::plain`, `image_tail` (for `MetaCodec::Stored`, the package's codec, a copy of `plain`), `BlockSource`'s on-disk blocks (the tail again, one 64 KiB `Vec` per block) and a clone of `plain` handed to `kraken_image::compress` (cloned twice more for the install metadata). It is now held once: `Metadata::image_tail()` returns the codec's container, or `plain` for a stored region (the field is private); `BlockSource::block` copies a metadata block out of it into its reused buffer, zero-padding a short last block as before; `BlockSource::metadata_region` borrows. The container's presentation artwork (`pic*.png`/`.dds`, up to 16 MiB each) was also held twice, in `Prepared` and in a clone for `StreamRequest`, which now borrows it (`extras: &[ExtraEntry]`). Same bytes: the block source test now covers both codecs. The Kraken pipeline keeps `threads × 2` blocks in flight, not `× 8` (still two per worker; 42 MiB less at 14 threads). Found on a 19 GB game (7,169 files, 897 folders): a 57 MiB region and 76 MiB of artwork, a 590 MiB heap peak while compressing, 794 MiB at the job's peak; now 478. |
| `0018-kraken-encoder-no-alloc-churn.patch` | The Kraken encoder allocates less per block, same bytes: `huffman_lengths` merges with two queues on stack arrays (the leaves sorted once by weight and index, merged nodes coming out in that order, so the merges are the heap's; a test checks against a heap), `huff::encoded_len` gives `encode`'s length without coding, so a half picks raw or delta literals by size and codes only the winner (it coded both), and the stream arrays, the Huffman streams and the offset bit writers are reserved whole instead of growing. Found on a PS5, whose libc serializes every malloc, realloc and free across threads: 4 compression threads on 32 MiB of a game's image ran at 13.1 MB/s, entropy coding taking 15x as long per block as on one thread; now 27.3 MB/s (one thread: 14.9). Same output on four 32 MiB samples (a `.pak` volume and three stretches of a 96 GB image). |
| `0019-package-without-eboot.patch` | `prepare` no longer refuses a source without `eboot.bin` ("the source has no eboot.bin"): by user decision such a package (additional content, an update) is built, `cnt_write::content_class` already giving it the additional-content class (0x21) when param.json names neither `applicationCategoryType` nor `applicationDrmType` (one that names a category gets 0x20 or 0x26). |
| `0020-package-output-trait.patch` | `build::write_package` writes into any `PkgOut` (`Read + Write + Seek + Send` with `try_clone_out`, `out_len`, `sync_out`), not only a `std::fs::File` (which implements it), so Forge can write a package onto another device. `write_mode`, `verify_written`, `stream::write_package` and `spool_file` take the trait (the in-place Kraken spool and the self-check read back through clones, each seeking first), and the header's FIH magic is written first, so an output that can't go back over its first byte (an FTP upload) takes the header written last; `fih::MAGIC` is `pub(crate)`; `kraken_image::compress` and `spool_block` are generic over `Write + Seek` / `Read + Seek`. Same bytes: a test builds one prepared package into a file and into an in-memory output whose clones share a buffer and compares them. |
| `0022-kraken-digest-in-memory.patch` | A plaintext Kraken build spooled in place (`KrakenSpool::InPlace`, what Forge uses) no longer reads its compressed image back from the output: `kraken_image::compress(.., digest_blocks, ..)` hands each stored 64 KiB block, as its bytes are written, to digest threads of its own (one per 8 compressing threads, at most 16 blocks queued) and returns every block's SHA3 and CRC32C in `KrakenImage::block_digests`, which `stream::write_package` takes for `imagedigs`, `playgo-chunk.crc` and the install metadata. An encrypted image (XTS-transformed after it is written) and a separate `File` spool (copied in) still read it back as before. For a package written onto another device this drops one full read of the image over the network before the self-check. Same bytes: the in-memory output test now runs plaintext and native, compares each with a file build, and counts the bytes read before `Stage::Verify` (none for plaintext); `compress`'s test checks the digests against the spool's blocks. |
| `0023-describe-each.patch` | `kraken_image::describe_each(blob, each)`: the descriptor walk `describe` does, with the same checks, handing each `DescribedBlock` (sparse zero blocks included) to `each` in mount order instead of collecting them (an error from `each` stops the walk); `describe` collects through it. Forge's reader keeps its own 32-byte block per block, so it no longer holds the 48-byte list (up to twice its length while it grew) beside its own: a 398 GiB package's 32 MB descriptor (issue #72) needed 410 MiB to open, now ~137 MB. Tests: `describe`'s own, which now run through it, and the reader's package round trip and damaged-descriptor tests (`crates/ps5-dump-forge-fpkg`). |
| `0024-trim-tests.patch` | Tests only, at the user's request to keep only the critical ones: 341 of 544 `#[test]` functions go (203 stay; 167 did before this rebase), with the helpers, `cfg(test)` modules, test files (`tests/pkg_source.rs`, `tests/ampr_pack.rs`) and fixtures (`tests/fixtures/ampr_pack`, `ampr_trace`, `pfs`, `ps4`) only they used. Gone: every test the v7.0.22 series' trim removed (the same names), and upstream's newer tests of code Forge doesn't use (PS4 packages and their merge, `pkg_source`, `browse`, the workshop's pause, the `.ffpfsc` writer, `finish`, `fself`, the `lih`/`protected` readers, the exFAT writer, `ampr_pack`, package kinds, PS3), of helpers and labels, and variants of a property another test keeps. Kept of upstream's newer ones: the Kraken 13-byte minimum, bad excess counts, entropy halves (Sony's zero halves, damage never panics); the gap tests (now zero blocks); exFAT root end and ValidDataLength; UFS2 null indirect pointers; the outer table loop, impossible dirents and a file capped by its image; the PFS reader's bounds and walks; PFSC crafted headers and mangling; case-only path collisions; `sample::pick`; the sampled CRC check and sampled sweep; param.json that isn't UTF-8, overflowing module offsets, a small file listed as huge, `packed_kind`; the runtime's AMPR index path limits; the game's own PlayGo languages; a content id with a path in it; and every test of `module_case` and `ffpfsc_compat`, which Forge calls (core's Unity module rename, its own `.ffpfsc` writer's `console_safe` guard). No code changes. |
| `0025-package-rules-languages-level3.patch` | Four package rules, by user request. (1) `sdk_rules::excluded` also leaves out a dumper's root `entitlements.txt` and `entitlement_key.dat`, a root `decrypted/` (host-side decryption copies), `.gp5-assets/` and `playgo-languages/` (a GP5 generator's inputs and its 1 MiB zero placeholder payloads, which come back in a package it built and was extracted) and `*/saved/config/*/*.ini` (an Unreal game's runtime settings). (2) Where the game's own `playgo-scenario.json` names no narrower list (upstream's `cnt_write::game_languages`), its own `playgo-chunk.dat` does when its chunks' language masks narrow them (`playgo::source_languages`: at most 1 MiB; each chunk's `u64` mask at attribute entry `+0x10`, bit 63 = ja-JP; every language or none: nothing to narrow), the default kept where it is one, else en-US, else the first. (3) Past level 2's 260,436,918,272 bytes the size class is level 3: `attributePub` 4 with `kernel.appSizeInGib` (the estimate in GiB, 256 through 320; the kernel object made or extended in place), where it declared level 2 before; not yet seen installing on a console. Every size class rewrite is read back (a text edit that landed on another key of the same name fails the build), and a param.json that isn't valid UTF-8 is left as it is (the edits cut bytes at text offsets). (4) `sdk_rules::notes` logs warnings that don't stop the build: a content ID off the PS5 pattern, an `icon0`/`pic0`/`pic1` PNG that isn't 8-bit RGB or a `pic2` that isn't 8-bit RGBA, and a `sce_sys/uds/udsNN.ucp` (at most 16 MiB) that isn't a plain UCP container or whose SHA-1 header digest (0x1C..0x30, zeroed for the hash) is stale. Adds `sha1` 0.11 (already in Forge's lock). Tests: the exclusions, level 3 into a kernel object and without one (and refused beside a top-level `appSizeInGib`), non-UTF-8 left alone, the language masks (narrowed, all, none, cut short), the content ID, PNG names and a UCP digest right and stale. |


drakmor's `ampr_emu` runtime is no longer vendored or embedded: `ps5-dump-forge-lz4` still recognises its builds in a game folder (`runtime::classify` by pinned SHA-256, `runtime::version_of`), and `scripts/check-lz4.sh` takes its 0.4.2.1 source archive from `AMPR_EMU_SRC`.

`ampr-emu-ng/` holds the unmodified ampr-emu-ng v0.5.1 release files (`libSceAmpr.sprx`, `SHA256SUMS`, `VERSION`; the release has no debug build here) and the tagged source archive; `ps5-dump-forge-lz4` embeds `libSceAmpr.sprx` (stored zstd-compressed by `crates/ps5-dump-forge-lz4/build.rs`, whose path names no version, so an upgrade replaces the files; decoded by `runtime::zstd()`); older builds, 0.4.1 included, are recognized by their pinned SHA-256 only; see its `README.md`.

## lzma-rust2

`lzma-rust2/` is the crates.io package `lzma-rust2` 0.22.0 (the version `sevenz-rust2` 0.24
resolves to; Apache-2.0, its `LICENSE` inside), as published, minus `.cargo-ok`,
`.cargo_vcs_info.json`, `.github/` and its `Cargo.lock` (the workspace lock pins its dependencies), plus one patch. The root `Cargo.toml` puts it in
`[patch.crates-io]` and leaves it out of the workspace (`exclude`), so `--workspace` lints and
tests don't cover it. Drop it once upstream bounds the decoder itself.

| Patch | What it does |
|---|---|
| `0021-lzma2-mt-bound-units-out.patch` | `Lzma2ReaderMt` kept dispatching work units while it waited for the next one in order, keeping every unit decoded ahead of it: one lagging worker let decoded data pile up without bound. It now dispatches only while fewer than two units per worker are out (dispatched, not yet returned), and a dropped reader drops its result receiver and joins its workers (each finishes its current unit), so no detached worker still holds buffers when the next reader starts. That bounds what `sevenz.rs` sizes its decode threads by (a dictionary and six runs per worker, inside a 256 MiB budget). Found on a solid 13.4 GB 7z: one thread took 143 s, 14 took 22 s at a 314 MiB peak. |

## License file

Upstream's `LICENSE` is the full GPL-3.0 text at `4174eee` (at the v7.0.22 base, `01afdf8`, it
was a truncated placeholder). `LICENSE-ps5upload` here is that file, unmodified (the same as this
repository's `LICENSE`). The grant is GPL-3.0-or-later, as upstream's notice and both
`Cargo.toml`s say.

## Checking and regenerating

The patches apply, in order, to a pristine upstream checkout and reproduce this folder exactly.
From this folder:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload /tmp/ps5upload
git -C /tmp/ps5upload checkout v12.6.30
rm -rf /tmp/series && mkdir /tmp/series
cp -R /tmp/ps5upload/engine/crates/ps5upload-fpkg /tmp/ps5upload/engine/crates/ps5upload-pkg /tmp/series/
(cd /tmp/series && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm pristine)
for p in patches/*.patch; do
    case $p in *0021-*) continue ;; esac
    (cd /tmp/series && git apply "$OLDPWD/$p" && git add -A && \
        git commit -qm "$(basename "$p" .patch | cut -d- -f2-)")
done
diff -r /tmp/series/ps5upload-fpkg ps5upload-fpkg && diff -r /tmp/series/ps5upload-pkg ps5upload-pkg
```

`/tmp/series` now holds the series as one commit per patch. To change patch N, copy the edited
crates over `/tmp/series`, `git commit --fixup <commit of patch N>`, then
`GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=: git rebase -i --autosquash <pristine commit>`; to add a patch, commit
it on top. Then write every patch again, each against its parent (`--full-index` without
`--binary`: the trim patch deletes binary fixtures, which `git apply` then checks by hash
instead of carrying their bytes; a patch that adds a binary file needs `--binary`):

```sh
cd /tmp/series && n=0
for c in $(git rev-list --reverse HEAD~$(($(git rev-list --count HEAD) - 1))..HEAD); do
    n=$((n + 1)); [ $n = 21 ] && n=22
    git diff --full-index --histogram "$c~1" "$c" > "$OLDPWD/patches/$(printf %04d $n)-$(git log -1 --format=%s "$c" | tr ' ' -).patch"
done
```

Number 0021 is lzma-rust2's patch (see lzma-rust2), so the series skips it.

Every patch state builds and passes its own tests; check with the gates below at each commit
when the series changes. Gates: `cargo fmt -p ps5upload-fpkg -p ps5upload-pkg --check`,
`cargo clippy -p ps5upload-fpkg -p ps5upload-pkg --all-targets` with no warnings, and
`cargo test -p ps5upload-fpkg -p ps5upload-pkg --release`.
